sourceQuotes: We compare the conventional baseline of TensorRT with CUDA graphs against multiple native megakernel and conventional graph design combinations. Each design runs at batch size 32 on H100 NVL GPU. Three megakernels (Figure 3) with overlap publish the first audio 4.05× sooner than conventional execution and 21.4% sooner than one megakernel design at batch size 32. The ordering holds at other batch sizes (Bn denotes batch size n): at B64, 47.4 ms against 61.0 ms for one megakernel and 221.5 ms for conventional; at B1, 27.5 ms against 32.7 and 73.0 ms respectively.

The frozen planner uniquely selected the measured fastest design in 13/13 held-out model-batch cases. This establishes selection accuracy within the declared validation pools across the tested workloads on H100 NVL. It does not establish optimality over unmeasured compositions or transfer to other GPU architectures.

NH-TTS reports the mean of per-batch request p95 TTFA over 36 batches in the main campaign. Qwen3-TTS computes p95 over three cohort-level first-PCM publication times per run and averages 9 run-p95 values across 3 processes at B1/B48/B64, or twelve across four processes at B16/B32. Llama computes p95 over 30 repetitions per process and aggregates across three processes using the arithmetic mean. We discard two warmup cohorts per process for NH-TTS, Qwen3-TTS and Llama, before measurement. Ratio confidence intervals use 20,000 bootstrap resamples of four matched GPU blocks for NH-TTS and Qwen3-TTS B16/B32, or nine matched process/run units for Qwen3-TTS B1/B48/B64, with paired resampling across designs. Collecting the planner’s inputs takes minutes: kernel benchmarks took 4.6 GPU-minutes for NH-TTS and 15.9 for Qwen3-TTS across four batch sizes.
